ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML/CFT Law, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Loi modifiée du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO Register Law, as amended); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés et le droit comptable; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; pertinent Grand-Ducal Regulations implementing the EU AML/CFT framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the SARL (Certificat d'immatriculation au RCS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministère de la Justice – Parquet Général (Luxembourg) or competent criminal record authority in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address for each UBO, manager, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular post, notary, or licensed professional of origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence includes screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001 and restrictive measures under the CFSP framework), (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) OFAC SDN List, and (iv) domestic Luxembourg CSSF guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs). Screening must be performed pre-signing, on incorporation, and continuously for the lifetime of the entity; results must be documented in the AML/CFT file maintained by the Luxembourg Professional in Financial Services (PFS) or notary.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal — https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script. French is the primary registry language; German is equally admissible. Names in other EU languages are accepted provided they use Latin characters and do not create confusion in the local market. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must not be misleading, unlawful, or contrary to public policy and must include an element distinguishing it from existing registered names. Use of 'Luxembourg' or 'Luxemburg' in a name requires justification and administrative acceptance; a non-resident or post-incorporation shell arrangement without genuine local substance may be refused.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the applicant may resubmit an amended name through the LBR portal within 30 days. If LBR refuses to register or reserve the name, a written reasoned appeal must be lodged with the Luxembourg Business Registers challenging the refusal decision. If rejected at LBR level, judicial recourse may be brought before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within the statutory time limit (generally three months from notification), through a Luxembourg-qualified Avocat à la Cour. The applicant should simultaneously preserve priority by filing a new name reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not permissible for a regulated NVOCC/freight-forwarding SARL. The entity must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg and sufficient tangible local substance (premises, equipment, local management, records), as required under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to regulated professions and the Commercial Code. Fully outsourced servicing through a licensed domiciliation agent is acceptable only at formation stage and must be progressively substantiated with local management, books and records, and decision-making presence; a shell-only configuration is prima facie incompatible with the freight-forwarding establishment authorization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high quantified risk of 45% within the first 24 months, driven by the medium-risk AML tier of ISIC 5229 (NVOCC ocean forwarding), frequent cash-equivalent flow, the Luxembourg dependence on UBO transparency, and the Ministry of the Economy's authority to conduct unannounced on-site inspections of licensed commercial establishments.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 23 June 2016 and the Law of 19 December 2020; SARL-specific regime under Articles 180-190; incorporation formalities and third-party effect under Articles 11-12; beneficial owner disclosure under the Law of 13 January 2019 (RBE Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), in coordination with the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg (Chamber of Notaries).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Deed of Incorporation (acte constitutif) filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000 under Articles 180-181 of the 1915 Act. Cash contributions must be deposited into a dedicated blocked corporate bank account in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the bank's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) must be delivered to the notary for attachment to the deed; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation report (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS' RESOLUTION — 15 January 2025. The undersigned sole manager, acting on the incorporation of LU SARL (the Company), hereby resolves: (1) Share Subscription — The initial share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed and paid in, evidenced by the bank blocking certificate annexed to the deed of incorporation; (2) Registered Office — The registered office of the Company is adopted at 12, Rue de l'Industrie, L-1810 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) Officers — The appointment of [Name] as authorised manager (gérant) is ratified, with full powers to open bank accounts, sign billing documents, supervise operational licensing and represent the Company before the RCS and tax authorities. The resolution is effective immediately and recorded in the corporate minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Verification and Notarisation of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — online name check portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal-entity name check on the LBR portal for the proposed corporate name; obtain a name reservation certificate where the chosen name is available; instruct a Luxembourg notary to draft the articles of incorporation; execute the acte constitutif in person before the notary, together with the bank blocking certificate and beneficial owner declarations; the notary authenticates the deed and assumes responsibility for onward RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of incorporators
Proof of residence of shareholders and managers
Draft articles of association
Luxembourg bank blocking certificate for EUR 12,000 minimum capital
AML/KYC declarations with corporate structure details
Name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR flags a conflicting name, file a written remark with the LBR within 5 business days and adopt a distinguishing suffix; if the notary queries the deed, execute an amending deed (acte rectificatif) before rehearing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Company in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); e-filing by the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the electronic registration dossier to the RCS within one month of the deed date, including the notarised deed, registered office consent, manager identification, and declarations of acceptance of office; pay the RCS inscription duty (approx. EUR 22 / USD 25); receive the RCS extract (extrait) and the national identification number (NID).
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation
Bank blocking certificate
Consent and specimen signatures of the gérant
Registered office agreement or lease
Beneficial owner declaration for the RBE register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, the notary corrects the entry and resubmits within 15 days; the company may submit a formal rectification request to the RCS under the Law of 19 December 2002 without penalty for non-contentious corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation in the RESA and Issuance of Third-Party Effect
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) publication service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transfers the registration to the RESA for publication; verify the published extract after one business day; the publication is the condition for opposability of the incorporation towards third parties; retain the RESA excerpt for bank, customs, and licensing files.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RESA publication voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains typographical errors, request an amended publication via the LBR portal; under Article 12 of the 1915 Act, corrections take effect retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Number Onboarding, Joint Social Security Registration and EORI Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the sole national identification number from the RCS to trigger VAT registration; complete VAT Form 301 for the intended taxable status; file contracts of the gérant and any employees with the CCSS using the registration declaration; apply for the EU EORI number through the customs Trader Portal to enable customs representation services for ocean freight and third-country consignments.
required_dossiers: RCS extrait dated within the last 3 months
VAT Form 301 pre-registration
National ID or residence permit of managers and staff
Bank account details
EORI application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late VAT registration, submit a spontaneous regularisation to AEDT with a request for remission of penalties; for EORI refusal, resubmit corrected identification data to the Administration des douanes et accises office in Luxembourg City.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Licensing as Transport Auxiliary (Freight Forwarding) and EU Customs Representation Authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics — Direction des transports; Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for the transport-auxiliary operating licence under the Law of 5 August 2001, demonstrating professional competence, financial standing (own funds of at least EUR 10,000 or equivalent), and good repute; obtain the customs representation authorisation under Article 39 of the Union Customs Code through the EU Trader Portal, proving financial solvency, absence of serious criminal convictions of the managers, and professional competence certified by diplomas or equivalent; after both authorisations are granted, the NVOCC may lawfully issue freight forwarding billing under the Luxembourg VAT framework; if operating in US ocean trades, additionally register with the US Federal Maritime Commission as a non-Vessel-Operating Common Carrier.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Transport auxiliary application form with proof of professional competence
Certificate of good conduct (casier judiciaire) for managers
Financial statements or bank solvency certificate
UCC Article 39 authorisation questionnaire and bonding evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry issues a suspension notice for missing financial evidence, submit additional bank certificates within 10 business days; any refusal is subject to hierarchical appeal to the Minister and annulment proceedings before the Tribunal administratif (Administrative Tribunal).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics — Direction des transports (Transport Licensing Directorate); Administration des douanes et accises (Customs and Excise Agency) for customs representation authorisations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'auxiliaire de transport (Transport Auxiliary / Freight Forwarding Operating Licence) under the Law of 5 August 2001, together with the UCC Article 39 Customs Representation Authorisation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Registration / Exempt; office-based NVOCC freight brokerage does not trigger a full environmental impact assessment under the Law of 15 June 2004 (EIA) on environmental impact assessment, as amended.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges apply. Office servitude compliance: separate collection and consignment of office waste under the Law of 21 March 2017; WEEE-compliant disposal of IT and telecom equipment; zero VOC emission threshold (no solvent-based operations); HVAC and refrigeration equipment subject to Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 on F-gases; noise emissions must not exceed 50 dB(A) at the office site boundary during night hours.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), including an on-site inspection and issuance of the safety attestation (attestation de sécurité incendie); structural load assessment of the registered office for document archives and container-file storage racks; workplace health and safety clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) under the Labour Code, comprising the mandatory general risk assessment (évaluation des risques), fire-exit planning, and first-aid organisation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct Taxation: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu). Indirect Taxation and VAT: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED), Luxembourg (portal: aed.public.lu). Customs: Administration des Douanes et Accises (ADT), Luxembourg (portal: douanes.public.lu). Unified digital front office: MyGuichet.lu (corporate registration) and MyTax.lu (electronic filing and assessment).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SARL through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); a 13-digit national identification number (n° d'identification) is automatically issued and functions as the corporate TIN. Step 2 — File VAT registration (form 640-F) with the AED via MyGuichet.lu; a non-established foreign entity must register before any taxable supply in Luxembourg (zero threshold) and appoint a Luxembourg-resident fiscal agent (représentant responsable solidaire) when no local establishment exists; the AED grants a VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits within approximately 15 business days. Step 3 — Obtain an EORI number from the ADT for customs declarations and register for excise or bonded-storage procedures if used. Step 4 — Register with the ACD for employer withholding (taxe sur les salaires) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) once staff or premises are located in Luxembourg. Step 5 — Activate MyTax.lu e-filing with a LuxTrust certificate and appoint a tax representative where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — The SARL is a Luxembourg tax-resident capital company taxed on worldwide profits: corporate income tax (IRC) at 17%, solidarity surcharge at 7% of IRC, municipal business tax (IBT) at 6.75% in Luxembourg City, yielding an aggregate headline rate of 24.94%; net wealth tax at 0.5% of net assets (EUR 500,000 allowance; SME growth allowance up to EUR 4.5 million). Pass-through status is unavailable; NVOCC freight-forwarding profits are fully allocated to the entity and are not within the Luxembourg tonnage-tax regime, which is reserved for qualifying vessel owners and operators.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Fiscal unity election (intégration fiscale, art. 164bis LIR) for groups holding at least 99% of Luxembourg subsidiaries, consolidating CIT and IBT after prior ACD approval with a minimum five-year commitment. No check-the-box regime; hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralised under the ATAD implementing Law of 21 December 2018. VAT group election (art. 62bis Loi TVA) permits closely linked Luxembourg entities to be treated as a single taxable person. Small business exemption election (art. 57 Loi TVA) applies where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000. Participation exemption election (art. 166 LIR) is available for qualifying shareholdings held through a Soparfi. Tax-neutral merger, demerger, and asset-transfer rollover elections are available under arts. 170–176 LIR.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-resident foreign entities: obligatory VAT registration from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg, with no turnover threshold. Resident small businesses: optional exemption under art. 57 Loi TVA up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover; mandatory registration above that amount. The reverse charge applies without threshold to freight and ancillary transport services purchased from non-resident carriers where the B2B place of supply is Luxembourg; the NVOCC must self-assess VAT under reverse charge and may recover the corresponding input VAT in the same return.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, API telemetry, or digital stamping. Business-to-government e-invoicing via Peppol BIS 3.0 (Factur-X/UBL) has been mandatory since 1 January 2022 for invoices issued to Luxembourg public-sector entities. B2B electronic invoicing is lawful upon recipient consent (art. 85(1) Loi TVA), including EDI or EN16931-compliant XML; paper and PDF equivalents remain acceptable. VAT returns (form 1074) are e-filed monthly for turnover above EUR 2 million, quarterly for turnover between EUR 112,000 and EUR 2 million, and annually for lower turnover, exclusively through MyTax.lu; recapitulative statements for intra-Community services are filed via the CSL system. All invoices and supporting records must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% rate (exemption with right to deduct, art. 44 Loi TVA) applies to: (1) exports of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the EU [art. 44(1)(a)]; (2) international transport of goods to a destination outside the EU [art. 44(1)(c)]; (3) freight-forwarding, brokerage, cargo handling, customs clearance, and other services directly connected to the export of goods [art. 44(3)–(6)]; and (4) ancillary services for goods in transit to non-EU destinations. An NVOCC zero-rates its ocean consolidation, booking, and handling fees where the consolidated cargo leaves the EU under a non-EU bill of lading; for international transport, the zero-rating is pro-rated by distance travelled outside the EU under the art. 17 place-of-supply rule for B2B services. Substantiation requires full export evidence, correct 0% VAT coding on invoices with the reference 'Exonération art. 44' and the export document number, and inward settlement of proceeds within the 180-day repatriation window. The reverse-charged VAT on vessel-operator freight purchases remains fully deductible against the zero-rated output.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — LU-CERT/ECS electronic export message with MRN, customs office of export, and date of exit from the EU
Bill of Lading — master or NVOCC house bill evidencing a non-EU consignee and a non-EU port of discharge
Inward Remittance Certificate — SWIFT MT103 or Luxembourg bank statement evidencing receipt of freight proceeds in EUR within 180 days of the payment request
Commercial Invoice and Packing List — HS codes, Incoterms, declared customs value, weight, and container references
Continuous Proof of Export — CMR road consignment notes for the pre-carriage leg to the EU port, T1 transit documents, exit summary message (EXS), and terminal loading lists
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED audits export zero-rating under the standard 5-year VAT limitation period, extended to 10 years where fraud is established. Any export voucher bundle that is incomplete — including absence of the inward remittance certificate within the 180-day window — is rejected; the VAT is retroactively clawed back and re-assessed at 17% with default interest at 5% per annum. Civil fines under art. 61 Loi TVA range from 10% of the VAT for formal negligence to 100% for deliberate concealment; invoicing, e-invoicing, and archiving breaches attract fines of EUR 750–25,000. The AED may impose joint and several liability on an NVOCC acting as fiscal agent for the VAT of non-registered foreign principals under art. 64 Loi TVA. Criminal sanctions under §397 of the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung) provide for imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to EUR 250,000 for fraudulent zero-rating claims by de jure or de facto officers. Refund claims are suspended during audit, and fraudulently obtained refunds are subject to immediate clawback with accrual of penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and the competent monetary authority for Luxembourg; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the licensing and AML/CFT supervisory authority for credit institutions, payment institutions, and e-money institutions; the European Central Bank (ECB) retains supranational competence for monetary policy and the Single Supervisory Mechanism for significant banks in the Eurozone.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is an integral member of the euro area, and euro (EUR) is fully convertible in both current and capital account transactions pursuant to Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). There is no foreign exchange control regime, no approval requirement for cross-border capital movements, and no restriction on dividend or profit remittance beyond standard corporate law solvency tests and the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (reducible under tax treaties). Resident banks report cross-border transactions to the BCL for Balance of Payments (BoP) statistical purposes, but reportability is not a permissioning hurdle. The SARL may maintain multi-currency accounts (EUR, USD, CNY, GBP) and freely repatriate operating profits after audit and tax clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed period for repatriation of receivables. Export and freight-forwarding income generated by the Luxembourg SARL may be retained in original invoice currency, converted at freely negotiated bank rates, or credited directly to a foreign-currency sub-account. The only statutory obligations are accurate BoP reporting to the BCL through the resident account-holding bank and full traceability of trade-related payments under the CSSF AML/KYC framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (ancillary treasury use only). Luxembourg recognizes EU-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2); their cross-border passporting into Luxembourg permits the holding of operational float, fee collection and outward disbursement execution. However, a digital EMI cannot lawfully serve as the primary treasury rail for a Luxembourg SARL because it cannot report BoP statistics to the BCL with the same statutory completeness as a licensed credit institution, and most EMIs decline capital subscription inflows, escrow mandates and documentary trade settlements. Non-EU offshore EMIs without a Luxembourg or EU passport are not viable and would expose the SARL to unlicensed activity risk under CSSF regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks apply CSSF AML/CFT circulars, including Circular 20/744 (KYC) and regulation requiring identification of all directors, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and signatories before onboarding. In-person KYC interviews are the de facto market standard for non-resident directors of newly formed SARLs: at minimum one director and one senior UBO must appear physically at a Luxembourg branch or at a recognized foreign group bank acting as introducer. Pure remote account opening is occasionally offered to EU-resident directors using CSSF-approved video-identification technology, subject to certified true (apostilled) corporate documentation and a risk-based call-back. For an NVOCC with cross-border freight flows, the onboarding bank will almost certainly mandate physical presence and a compliance interview in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layer holding chain with intermediate Luxembourg or foreign corporate entities obscuring UBO chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Excerpt of Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), full corporate organizational chart, notarized statutes of each layer, UBO identification form, and a written source-of-wealth narrative covering capital formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected transaction profile inconsistent with declared NVOCC activity (high-frequency payments to ports, ocean carriers and overseas agents)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed freight forwarding contracts, pro-forma invoices, sample bills of lading, Customs or SCAC/FMC registration evidence, and a 12-month cash-flow forecasting model with counterparty geographies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus in outbound freight payments (e.g., sanctioned ports, OFAC/EU-listed counterparties)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening output, counterparty due diligence files (licenses, ultimate owners), end-user undertakings, country risk assessment memo, and a cargo transit documentation packet evidencing lawful exports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags, including invoice over/under-invoicing or circular settlement structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent valuation of freight charges, audited commercial ledgers, matching of SWIFT beneficiary names to voyage charter agreements, and bank references attesting to the SARL's operating history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficiently verified non-EU director or UBO identity / lack of legalized documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passports and proof of address notarized and apostilled under the Hague Convention, bank and professional references from prior financial institutions, CSSF-compliant ID verification on video conference, and certified translation of all corporate documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital injection from the EU parent or third-country shareholder must be executed via SWIFT MT103 (outside SEPA) or SEPA Credit Transfer (within SEPA) to the SARL's designated EUR operational account at the Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. The beneficiary bank will require the payment reference 'Share capital subscription — SARL [name], capital increase resolution [date]', supported by a notarized notarial deed of incorporation or capital increase minutes, a bank statement of the remitter, and a completed BoP purpose declaration (ECB/BCL statistical code, typically D.1.3 for direct investment equity capital). There is no exchange control authorization; the bank opens the account upon completion of its KYC and RBE verification. The funds can be retained in EUR or converted to USD at the SARL's discretion, and no statutory surrender rule applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are settled through (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-EU and non-SEPA counterparties, principally payments to ocean carriers, overseas NVOCC partners, port authorities and foreign customs brokers; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer for EU payment recipients, using ISO 20022 XML (pain.001) formats harmonized under the ECB's November 2025 single EURO payment area message standard; and (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Luxembourg relationship bank for large-volume, documentary freight and charter commitments where the carrier requires a bank undertaking. All disbursements must be matched against underlying invoices, bills of lading, and shipping contracts to satisfy both CSSF AML controls and the SARL's own treasury verification matrix.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards — fully permissible for hedging the SARL's ocean freight receivables and carrier disbursement mismatch, with execution under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or local confirmations.
FX swaps and spot-forward combinations for short-term rolling of USD, EUR, GBP and CNY positions during voyage settlement cycles.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CSS) on EUR/USD or EUR/GBP for converting long-term vessel-contract liabilities into functional currency.
Vanilla FX options (puts/calls) on EUR/USD permitted for purchased freight margin protection, subject to CSSF conduct-of-business and IFRS hedge accounting documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to receivables or payables denominated in non-deliverable or restricted currencies (e.g., onshore CNY or INR) where a corresponding ordinary deliverable forward is structurally unavailable; such NDFs must be entered into only with the licensed Luxembourg bank or an EU-authorised investment firm and reported under EMIR with appropriate underlying trade documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via eCDF platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year end; 31 July for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine €300 plus €25 per day up to €3,600; persistent default triggers court-ordered compulsory strike-off and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the tax year; extension to 30 June/30 September available upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 10% p.a.; administrative fines up to €3,750 or 10% of unpaid tax; collection enforcement on continued non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as CIT: 31 March of the following year (extendable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €2,500; 10% late-payment interest; mandatory increase for repeated default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of the initial UBO filing date; annual cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties up to €20,000 per entity; additional fines for inaccurate or outdated information; possible court order to regularize

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Exceed two of three tests for two consecutive years: total assets €4.4M, net turnover €8.8M, average employees 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Directive-compliant); IFRS as adopted by EU permissible for unlisted entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually confirm UBO data via RBE portal within one month of registration anniversary; any change (including share transfers) must be submitted within 15 days; non-compliance is criminally sanctioned

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective headline corporate rate for Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax + 7% employment-fund surcharge on CIT)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption for qualifying IP income; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity; no Luxembourg withholding tax on royalties or interest; loss carryforward indefinitely with annual cap of 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: indefinite; annual offset limited to 50% of taxable income above EUR 1,000,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 1 (IRC/ICC/IF) filed electronically via eCDF (déclaration électronique des collectivités) on impotsdirects.public.lu or MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly CIT prepayments due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the tax year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December immediately following the calendar tax year-end; for a SARL with a 31 December year-end, the FY2024 return is due by 31 December 2025

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, R.C.S. Luxembourg registration number, matricule number, registered office, legal form (SARL), main NACE/ISIC activity (5229 - ocean freight forwarding/NVOCC)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State only the Luxembourg resident entity; identify all non-resident shareholders with country, tax identification number and percentage ownership

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the financial year and number of days in the tax period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly incorporated SARL, state incorporation date and confirm first taxable period; non-resident shareholders need take no entry

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Cadre C - Siège et administration centrale
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address where central management and control, decisions, bookkeeping and freight-forwarding operations are effectively carried out
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must report whether management decisions are taken in Luxembourg; if decision-making is abroad, risk of foreign permanent establishment or Luxembourg residence challenge

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Cadre D - Bilan et compte de profits et pertes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit-and-loss account prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in EUR, including revenue from NVOCC container brokerage, forwarding fees, ancillary logistics services and operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income of the Luxembourg SARL; no separate form for non-resident shareholders unless they hold a Luxembourg permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit before loss carryforward and after addbacks, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, excessive or inadequate director fees, interest limitation adjustments and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent must document intercompany charges using Luxembourg arm's-length rules; absent documentation the tax authority may disallow freight, booking and container procurement costs

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available loss carryforwards, loss used in the current year and remaining carryforward balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter carryforward schedule only for the Luxembourg SARL; non-resident shareholders cannot use SARL losses on their own tax returns

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Cadre G - Exonérations, déductions et crédits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption on qualifying dividends/capital gains, IP box deduction, notional interest deduction, foreign tax credits, and any maritime/ocean transport treaty-specific allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent claiming treaty credit on Luxembourg-profits must obtain and retain a Luxembourg tax residence certificate for the SARL; no offset is allowed at field level

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Cadre H - Calcul de l'IRC
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax, employment-fund surcharge and municipal business tax on the taxable base allocated to Luxembourg City
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the municipal territory (Luxembourg City) where the freight-forwarding activity is physically exercised; a non-resident NVOCC without a Luxembourg PE has no Luxembourg CIT liability

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 1, Cadre I - Déclaration et signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the authorised SARL manager, date and signature; digital signature on eCDF confirms liability under penalty of perjury
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director/manager may sign if formally appointed; personal signature triggers joint liability for false declarations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a late-payment surcharge of up to 10% of tax due, monthly interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax, default assessment by the tax office, and possible administrative fine; intentional non-filing is prosecuted as tax fraud with fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months; treaty rates for non-EU shareholders range from 0% to 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, obtain a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax authority and submit it to the Luxembourg paying agent before distribution together with an ownership and holding-period declaration; if tax is withheld at the 15% domestic rate, the non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim with the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) attaching the TRC, dividend voucher and relevant treaty provisions
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties; statutory domestic rate is 0%; most Luxembourg double tax treaties also provide 0% withholding on interest and royalties, subject to substance and beneficial ownership requirements

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: National Master File/Local File expectation for Luxembourg taxpayers with more than 150 employees and annual turnover exceeding EUR 50,000,000 or balance-sheet assets exceeding EUR 43,000,000; mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000; smaller NVOCC SARLs must still maintain contemporaneous documentation for intercompany freight, management and financing transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no separate Economic Substances Regulation comparable to UAE law, but Article 6 of the Luxembourg Tax Adjustment Act (Steueranpassungsgesetz), the Luxembourg GAAR and BEPS treaty-abuse rules require real economic substance; the NVOCC SARL must maintain an office, employees, contracts, client-facing freight operations and management decisions in Luxembourg to access tax treaties, the participation exemption and 0% withholding tax benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating ocean freight revenue, issuing false NVOCC invoices, omitting container brokerage income, suppressing Luxembourg-source profits, falsifying books or submitting a fraudulent eCDF return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax assessment of up to 50% of the evaded tax, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; criminal conviction for tax fraud may result in fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors who sign or direct false returns are personally liable for civil restitution of unpaid tax and may face sequestration, travel bans and imprisonment; corporate veil may be pierced on evidence of fraudulent abuse

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Luxembourg SARL acting as an invoicing conduit with no physical office, no employees, no freight-forwarding contracts and no management substance; overseas parent books containers while the SARL merely issues invoices and passes profits to non-resident shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax authorities may disregard the SARL's separate existence, recharacterise transactions, deny treaty benefits, disallow deduction of intercompany costs, treat distributions as hidden profit-sharing and reassess CIT plus 15% withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for the reassessed taxes if they knowingly operated a sham entity; travel bans and director disqualification can be imposed in serious cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length allocation of ocean freight forwarding margin, inflated management fees, excessive container procurement commissions, unrealistic low profitability in Luxembourg, insufficient TP documentation for intercompany logistics services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to arm's-length taxable profit, additional CIT and municipal business tax, 0.6% monthly late-payment interest and accuracy-related penalties; intentional mispricing is treated as fraudulent tax evasion with fines and imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve tax-motivated intercompany pricing without economic substance or documentation expose themselves to personal liability for resulting tax deficiencies and criminal penalties for intentionally false TP documents

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax evasion and dividend stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding 15% or without meeting the 10% / 12-month Parent-Subsidiary Directive holding condition; arranging artificial holding chains solely to obtain 0% withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid 15% dividend withholding tax plus interest; anti-abuse recharacterisation of the distribution; penalty of up to 50% of the evaded withholding tax and potential criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for withheld taxes that they intentionally fail to remit; they may be subject to restitution orders, penalties and imprisonment for breach of fiduciary duty

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing SWIFT or ACH payments through shell counterparties, using forged bills of lading, moving goods to sanctioned jurisdictions, accepting cash without AML due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions, or knowingly facilitating trade-based money laundering through the NVOCC platform
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; freezing of assets; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering; revocation of NVOCC licences and bank access
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and AML responsible persons may be personally liable for failures in customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting; personal fines, professional disqualification and travel bans may be imposed
